blocks.prompt: 6. [printed as 5.] Find the area bounded by the parabola \(x = 9 - y^{2}\), and the \(y\)-axis.
blocks.explanation:
Yahan curve \(x\) ke roop mein \(y\) ka function hai (\(x = 9 - y^{2}\)), yani parabola left-right khulta hai, upar neeche nahi.
Region \(y\)-axis ke saath band hai, is liye horizontal (letti hui) strips lena aasaan hai: \(A = \int_c^d x\,dy\) (3.7.1 ka Note 4).
Plan: parabola \(y\)-axis ko kahan kaatta hai (yeh \(y\)-limits hain), phir \(y\) ke lehaaz se integral.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x = 9 - y^{2}\) aur \(y\)-axis (yani \(x = 0\)).
Maloom karna: band area.
Tareeqa: \(A = \int_c^d f(y)\,dy\), jahan \(y = c\) se \(y = d\) tak \(f(y) \ge 0\) ho. Yeh wohi formula hai jo hum \(x\) ke liye use karte hain, bas axes ka kirdar badal gaya hai.

Qadam 1: \(y\)-axis par limits
\[9 - y^{2} = 0 \Rightarrow y = \pm 3\]
Kyun: \(y\)-axis par \(x = 0\) hota hai, is liye \(x = 0\) rakh kar milne ke points mile: \((0, 3)\) aur \((0, -3)\). In ke darmiyan \(x = 9 - y^{2} \ge 0\), yani region \(y\)-axis ke dayen taraf hai.
Dhyan dein: Is sawal mein \(x\)-limits dhoondhne ki koshish ghalat raasta hai; curve \(x = f(y)\) ki shakal mein hai to limits bhi \(y\) ki hongi.

Qadam 2: \(y\) ke lehaaz se integrate karein
\[A = \int_{-3}^{3}(9 - y^{2})\,dy = 2\int_0^3 (9 - y^{2})\,dy\]
\[= 2\left[9y - \dfrac{y^{3}}{3}\right]_0^3 = 2(27 - 9) = 36\]
Kyun: \(9 - y^{2}\) mein \(y\) ki jagah \(-y\) rakhne se kuch nahi badalta (even function), is liye \([-3, 3]\) ka integral \([0, 3]\) ke integral ka double hai. Power rule: \(\int y^{2}dy = \frac{y^{3}}{3}\).

Tasdeeq:
Archimedes ka purana rule: parabola ka segment apne ird gird wale rectangle ka \(\frac{2}{3}\) hota hai. Yahan rectangle ki chaurai 9 aur lambai 6 hai: \(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 54 = 36\). Dono tareeqon se ek hi jawab aaya, is liye jawab sahi hai.
